Get a couple of pieces of paper towel, spray Windex a couples of times on the paper towel, then put a coffee filter over the paper towel. Use that to clean your screen, keyboards, mice. Works great, leaves no lint, and you don't ever get to much Windex on the machine.

Don't stop too soon.

You don't actually "clean" glass - you polish it. It's like waxing a car or polishing silver - you have to buff out the smudges.

Use a mild cleaner (eyeglass cleaner is safe and effective, or a cheaper alternative is a solution of distilled water, dish detergent and vinegar) and a soft, lint-free cloth. Spray a light mist of cleaner on the surface, then wipe the entire surface down to remove most of the cleaner. The important thing is to not stop there. Keep going over the surface, lightly buffing to remove the streaks. And keep rotating the cloth (or use another cloth if necessary) so that you're constantly using a dry surface - if the part of the cloth you're using is itself damp, then it'll just drag smears around with it, over and over. Keep doing that and you'll eliminate all the streaks.
